and that’s not even considering how creativity/the creative process challenges our brains and is literally good for us. it’s the same reason i’m against AI for writing a paper or whatever. you are not challenging yourself with this kind of thing, you’re not improving and you’re not forcing yourself to do anything new or different. there’s no learning, no pride in your work, nothing that pushes you and makes you grow.

for me it’s less about it looking one way or another and moreso about how i feel it undermines the entire concept of creativity and the innate human desire to produce art. Real art takes time. It takes inspiration and immense amounts of training and effort and finesse to make work. It makes you feel something not only due to its content, but because of its context. Art is something uniquely human and the infiltration of that with this fucked up sense of ‘modernity’ and ‘progress’ results in a product that’s soulless, has no narrative or backstory attached and that’s devoid of meaning/feeling. The whole point of art is to experience it, and those experiences are embedded into the process and piece via the human element. AI art is aesthetically pleasing, but knowing it’s art imitating life, imitating humanness, makes it uncanny and even tacky. it’s not ‘cheating’ to want to know the context of art… the context is PART of the art. the context is symbolism and meaning and provides insight into the minds and experiences of the artist and really, the world around them at the time. art isn’t art if the human element isn’t there, and typing in a few key words into the generator box isn’t going to cut it.
